properties.decision:
reflow2's own decomposition is the functional systems a design-graph tool IS — foundation, vocabulary, store, coherence-loop, human-channel, time-history, intake, agent-surface, documentation, packaging — with the Rust modules re-parented under them as implementation. The as-built crate grouping (reflow2-core / -mcp / kit) is retired from the as-designed view.

CORRECTED 2026-08-02: this said "the seven functional systems" and named seven. There were EIGHT — `sys:documentation` joined later under `dec:documentation-has-no-operational-coupling`, which accepts that documentation is part of the product while having no operational coupling, so it forms an island the detectors are told to expect. The choice this decision records was unchanged; only its enumeration had gone stale, which is why that was a correction on the record rather than a superseding decision (`dec:reopen-supersedes` governs reversals, not arithmetic). Found by re-measuring a claim rather than re-reading it: the decision's prose said seven while `scan_nodes` said eight.

AMENDED 2026-08-20, and THIS ONE IS NOT ARITHMETIC. There are now NINE. `sys:foundation` was CREATED under `dec:the-kernel-is-its-own-system` (accepted, Anthony's word) and holds cmp:nodes, cmp:schema, cmp:graph, cmp:provenance and cmp:identity — five modules that had been split across `sys:vocabulary` and `sys:store`, with identity in no system at all. Unlike the 2026-08-02 correction, the carving itself moved: a system exists now that did not exist before. It does not overturn this decision, it follows from it — a design-graph tool fundamentally IS a typed store of identified nodes, and that is one function, not two halves of two. The bisection was measured, not argued: it was the entire cause of a `sys:store` <-> `sys:vocabulary` cycle, while the modules themselves are acyclic (`fact:the-modules-are-acyclic-but-the-declared-subsystems-are-not`).

THE COUNT THAT WAS NOT WRONG, recorded so nobody "fixes" it twice: the 14 distinct cross-system pairs cited in `dec:maturity-restructuring-delta` are DIRECTED pairs; counted undirected the same 51 edges span 12. Both are right, they answer different questions, and the recorded figure means directed.

AMENDED AGAIN 2026-08-20, same day, on Anthony's word: there are now TEN. `cmp:packaging` — how reflow2 SHIPS: the per-platform binary matrix, the consumer kit and its manifest, the install and update path, the container image — is PROMOTED from a leaf component to a subsystem. It had been floating at the root of the spine declaring itself a leaf, which is why "what are the top-level parts?" answered differently by declared level than by position. Promotion rather than placement-under-something because the graph says it is real and finished: four capabilities, three of them realized, with `art:release-workflow` behind them, serving accepted intent in `req:frictionless-update`. Something that shipped is not scaffolding.

ITS ID KEEPS THE `cmp:` PREFIX AND THAT IS COSMETIC, recorded so nobody reads meaning into it. The other nine carry `sys:`. reflow2 has no rename operation, and fabricating a migration to a new id would destroy the node's snapshot history for a prefix. The `level` property is what the hierarchy computation reads; the prefix is a naming habit that predates the promotion.

ALSO IN THIS EPOCH, and it is a PLACEMENT rather than a change to the carving: `cmp:registry` was moved inside `sys:agent-surface`. It had no parent at all. Its three capabilities are unbuilt and nothing realizes it, and its own description says the per-graph state it will own "today rides on ReflowService as per-process state" — so the agent surface is where that function actually lives. Modelling it as a peer of the ten would claim a separation that has not happened yet. When the hosted tier is real it can be promoted, and `move_component` makes that one call.
properties.name: reflow2's systems are functional, not its file tree
properties.rationale: The self-model had been recovered backwards from the file tree, so its 38 Components were the Rust module list and the domain primitives a design-graph product fundamentally is — node and edge types — appeared nowhere (BL-83). A functional carving comes from the product's purpose (a genesis input), not the code, and cuts across crate boundaries, so adopt on the code can only re-derive the module view. Derived with the user, 2026-07-23. The retired crate view is recovered by adopt-on-a-copy (BL-83b) and the divergence measured by compare_designs (BL-83c). A SECOND GAP FELL OUT OF THE CORRECTION AND IS WORTH MORE THAN IT: the snapshot taken before the edit showed only SEVEN `GOVERNED_BY` edges into this decision, so `sys:documentation` was carrying no link to the decomposition that defines it — the eighth system existed in the graph while being invisible to anything traversing from this decision. Now linked, matching its seven siblings. Per sharpening §2 that edge is completing the model rather than silencing a complaint: the system genuinely is part of this decomposition, and nothing was reporting its absence.
